# AGENTS.md — GitHub Actions

Run jobs on Windows runners (`windows-*` labels) under native `pwsh`. Native Windows pull-request jobs live in `ci-windows.yml` and Python pull-request jobs in `ci-python.yml`, so each PR workflow can be re-run independently; their checks feed the required `windows checks passed` and `python checks passed` verdicts, as Linux jobs in `ci.yml` feed `all checks passed`; Wine runs Windows Node on hosted Linux only in `ci-master.yml`. Python runtime CI checks Linux/Windows x64 on pull requests and Linux ARM64 plus both macOS architectures on master pushes; releases retain all five targets ([platform policy](workflows/ci-master.yml)). `ci.yml`, `ci-windows.yml`, and `ci-python.yml` are pull-request-only. Master-only platform checks, Linux/Windows self-hosted standbys, and manual runner benchmarks live in `ci-master.yml`, which listens to master pushes and `workflow_dispatch`, not `pull_request`; separating workflow triggers keeps master-only jobs out of PR check panels. The master standbys validate the self-hosted failover targets; preserve the existing per-platform switches (values `selfhosted` for the in-house standbys and `blacksmith` for Blacksmith's hosted runners) and the Dependabot hosted fallback under the `selfhosted` values ([failover runbook](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-ci-failover-runbook.md), [blacksmith failover leg note](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-09-09-blacksmith-failover-leg.md)).

The manual [Windows packaging workflow](workflows/windows-package.yml) uses the dedicated self-hosted Windows x64 label `dsh-win-package-trial` under native `pwsh`; preserve this routing separately from the automatic CI lanes.

The merge checks run from three workflows named `Policy`, which run on `pull_request_target` so their definitions come from master, and call the `deepseek-harness-check` action directly: `pr-check-on-head-branch.yml` on pull-request updates gives `Policy / Master Change` and `Policy / Pre-Merge Check`, `pr-check-after-approve.yml` on pull-request updates and submitted or dismissed reviews gives `Policy / Approve Check` and `Policy / Reviewer Evaluate`, and `pr-check-on-base-branch.yml` on master pushes re-runs the head-branch checks as `Policy / Recheck`. Branch rules require those check names, so keep the job names and the workflow name. Each check reads its mode from a repository variable: `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF`, `MERGE_POLICY_PRE_MERGE`, `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF`, and `MERGE_POLICY_REVIEW`, each `off` (skip), `report` (run without failing the job), or `block` (fail the job); a missing value or an unknown one counts as `report`. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` merges the commit `Policy / Master Change` reports, so it runs only after that job and stays off while `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF` is `off`; a merge it cannot do and a build that fails both follow its own mode, so `report` warns and skips the build while `block` fails the job. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` runs `scripts/pre-merge-check.ts` under plain Node and knows nothing else about the merged tree: that script checks the released manifests against the root version, installs, and builds the Host and Client contracts, so change it in one pull request together with the build it orchestrates.

The manual Desktop publication workflow selects a successful package run and attempt, then routes each retained build through `DESKTOP_PUBLISH_RUNNERS` to its original machine's unique label. Keep Windows run steps on native PowerShell and Mac run steps on the default POSIX shell; shared entrypoints are Node scripts. Test and production jobs use separate `desktop-test` and `desktop-production` approval Environments after a credential-free preparation job.
